title: Shared light and dry-air weights permitted only small August ozone reversals on two grids in North Wales in 2021
abstract: We extended a prior ozone ranking test to shared weights that increase with light and decrease with air dryness. Exact bounds on two nested grids used 1,464 August and September hours from a North Wales wildflower experiment in 2021. August concentration maxima were +0.001237 and +0.007981 ppb at two targets. Each selected one hour; removing the highest-light hour removed both reversals. September allowed no positive contrast. Nine smooth responses gave no reversal. Independent linear programs agreed with all bounds. This limits an extension of the prior dry-air-only claim, but gives no stable evidence of greater absorbed ozone. One site-year, unreplicated chambers, shared ambient weather, sensor uncertainty and finite grids limit inference. Independent regions and years remain untested. Original code, aggregate evidence, source hashes and external retrieval instructions are included.

display.caption: Largest recorded heated-minus-ambient concentration summaries over common light and VPD weights on two nested grids. These are exact grid bounds, not confidence intervals or absorbed doses.

citations.reason: We test the open extension from VPD-only weights to shared light and VPD weights. No code or derived data reused.
Exposure window audit supports exclusion of October.
